security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, examples, placeholders, and style-guide text. The real issue is command injection risk in validate_notebook.py where the detect-secrets command is built with sh -c and interpolated notebook paths.

remediation.issue: Shell command injection risk in detect-secrets validation
remediation.suggestion: Replace sh -c string construction with a direct subprocess argv list. Avoid echo and xargs, or quote all path arguments with shlex.quote.

remediation.issue: External validation tools are invoked during review
remediation.suggestion: Document that the validator runs uv, nbconvert, and detect-secrets. Prefer pinned tool versions and clear user confirmation before running checks.

content.user_title: Audit Cookbook Notebooks With a Rubric
content.value_statement: Cookbook notebooks need consistent checks before publication, and manual review often misses repeated style and setup problems. This skill combines automated validation with a rubric so reviewers can deliver specific, scored feedback.
actual_capabilities: Runs automated validation checks on Jupyter notebook files.
Converts notebooks to markdown for easier manual review.
Checks notebooks for hardcoded secrets with detect-secrets or fallback patterns.
Evaluates introductions, setup sections, code explanations, model constants, and conclusions.
Produces scored audit reports with strengths, issues, and concrete recommendations.
Applies the included Anthropic Cookbook style guide during review.
limitations: It supports Jupyter notebook files and does not review arbitrary document formats.
It does not execute notebook cells to verify runtime correctness.
Automated checks do not replace human review of pedagogy and technical accuracy.
Full validation depends on local tools such as uv, nbconvert, and detect-secrets.

use_cases.title: Review notebooks before publication
use_cases.description: Check submitted notebooks against style, setup, model, and secret-handling standards before merging or publishing.

use_cases.title: Standardize review feedback
use_cases.description: Use the scoring rubric to compare narrative quality, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability across submissions.

use_cases.title: Self-audit draft examples
use_cases.description: Find missing explanations, noisy setup cells, weak conclusions, and unsafe credential examples before requesting review.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this notebook with cookbook-audit: [path]. Run the automated checks, then summarize critical issues and warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Score Against the Rubric
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [path] against the Cookbook style guide. Include scores for narrative quality, code quality, technical accuracy, and actionability.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Setup and Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Focus on setup and security for [path]. Check prerequisites, API key handling, model constants, package installs, and secret detection results.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Drafts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [notebook_a] and [notebook_b] with cookbook-audit. Explain score differences, recurring issues, and the highest value revisions for each notebook.

output_examples.input: Audit a draft notebook for publication readiness.
output: Strengths: clear problem framing and useful examples.
Critical issues: missing conclusion and one weak setup explanation.
Recommended action: add learning objectives and map the recap back to them.

output_examples.input: Review only setup quality and secret handling.
output: Automated checks completed with no hardcoded secrets found.
Warnings: two adjacent code cells need explanatory text.
Setup guidance should mention required tools and keep the model name in one constant.

output_examples.input: Compare two notebooks from the same cookbook section.
output: Notebook A has stronger narrative structure and clearer prerequisites.
Notebook B has cleaner code presentation but lacks transfer guidance.
Revise Notebook B first because its conclusion and objectives are incomplete.

best_practices: Run automated validation before manual review so technical issues are visible early.
Use line-specific examples from the notebook when explaining every major finding.
Score each rubric dimension separately before writing the executive summary.
anti_patterns: Skipping the style guide and relying only on personal writing preferences.
Accepting placeholder API key patterns without checking whether they teach unsafe habits.
Giving generic feedback without concrete notebook references or next actions.

faq.question: Does this skill edit my notebook?
faq.answer: No. It reads the notebook, creates a markdown review copy, and returns audit feedback.

faq.question: Which file types are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow is designed for Jupyter notebook files with the .ipynb extension.

faq.question: Does it execute notebook cells?
faq.answer: No. The validator inspects notebook content and converts it to markdown for review.

faq.question: What automated checks are included?
faq.answer: It checks secrets, introductions, package install output, code explanations, variable names, model constants, deprecated patterns, and conclusions.

faq.question: Do I still need manual review?
faq.answer: Yes. Human review is still needed for narrative quality, pedagogy, technical judgment, and usefulness.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Full validation expects Python, uv, nbconvert, and detect-secrets or its fallback secret patterns.
